issues.legal_issue: A retrospective amendment validating assessments made by an additional revenue officer with the powers of a collector makes that officer competent to assess agricultural income tax.
material_facts: An additional revenue officer had been given the powers and duties of a collector and assessed agricultural income tax on an assessee whose agricultural property was in more than one district.
The High Court quashed the assessment for want of authority to assess property across districts.
After the High Court's judgment, the legislature retrospectively amended the agricultural income-tax law to include additional collectors and validate qualifying assessments.
issues.conclusion: The additional collector was competent to assess the assessee's liability to agricultural income tax and super-tax.
issues.legal_principle: Under the United Provinces Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1949, as amended by the United Provinces Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1956, an additional collector appointed and invested with the powers of a collector under the United Provinces Land Revenue Act, 1901, was included within the meaning of collector, and qualifying assessments were deemed valid at all material times. The Court relied on sections 2(4-a) and 10 of the amending Act and section 14(A) of the Land Revenue Act; it cited no earlier cases for this holding.

predicates.appeal_from_quashed_assessment: An appeal is brought against a judgment that quashed an assessment for lack of authority.
predicates.additional_officer_had_collector_powers: The officer who made the assessment had been given the powers and duties of a collector.
predicates.retrospective_law_validated_assessment: The legislature enacted a retrospective change that included such an officer and validated the assessment.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an assessment quashed for lack of authority, and the assessing officer had collector powers and a retrospective legislative change validates the assessment, the officer is treated as competent to assess.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court must apply a retrospective amendment enacted before the appeal is heard when it confers on the original authority jurisdiction that it previously lacked.
material_facts: The appeal was properly before the Supreme Court after the High Court had quashed the assessment for want of jurisdiction.
Before the appeal was heard, the legislature retrospectively amended the law to validate assessments by the additional officer and confer the authority he had previously lacked.
issues.conclusion: The Court was required to decide the appeal under the amended law as it stood at the hearing, including its retrospective effect.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate court must give effect to the law as it stands at the hearing when an earlier amendment operates retrospectively to confer on the authority whose order is under appeal jurisdiction that it originally lacked. The Court relied on the retrospective provisions of the United Provinces Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1949, as amended by the 1956 amending Act; it cited no earlier cases for this principle.

predicates.appeal_pending_before_appellate_court: An appeal is properly before an appellate court.
predicates.retrospective_amendment_preceded_hearing: A legislative amendment enacted before the appeal is heard operates retrospectively.
predicates.amendment_conferred_missing_authority: The retrospective amendment gives the authority whose order is appealed jurisdiction it previously lacked.

issues.definition: If an appeal is pending and a retrospective amendment enacted before its hearing confers previously missing jurisdiction, the appellate court applies that amendment in deciding the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory procedure for review does not restrict an appellate court's power to decide a properly pending appeal under a retrospective amendment.
material_facts: The amending Act provided for review of certain decisions setting aside assessments made by additional collectors.
The State sought review of the High Court's judgment, but the High Court rejected the application as not maintainable under that review provision.

The State's appeal was properly before the Supreme Court, which considered the effect of the retrospective amendment without deciding whether the High Court was right to reject the review application.
issues.conclusion: The review provision did not affect the Supreme Court's power to decide the appeal in light of the retrospective amendment.
issues.legal_principle: A review provision such as section 11 of the United Provinces Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1956, does not displace or impair an appellate court's power to decide an appeal properly before it under the law as retrospectively amended. The Court expressed no opinion on the correctness of the High Court's ruling on the maintainability of the review application and cited no earlier cases for this principle.

predicates.appeal_pending_before_appellate_court: An appeal is properly before an appellate court.
predicates.retrospective_amendment_applies: A retrospective amendment governs the dispute being considered on appeal.
predicates.review_procedure_is_provided: The legislature has provided a procedure to seek review of certain decisions affected by the amendment.

issues.definition: When a retrospective amendment applies to a dispute in a properly pending appeal, the existence of a statutory review procedure does not restrict the appellate court's power to decide the appeal under that amendment.
